provenance.task: Single-cell computation/learning/memory: does one cell with no nervous system compute/learn/remember? (empirical leg of the F254 conjecture; skeptical pole held)

findings.item: Stentor 2019 - behavioral hierarchy / sequential decision (NOT learning)
findings.claim: Dexter, Prabakaran & Gunawardena (2019, Current Biology) confirmed a hierarchical, sequential avoidance-response program in the single-celled ciliate Stentor ROESELI (correcting prior misidentification as S. coeruleus): the stereotyped sequence is bending -> ciliary alteration -> contraction -> detachment, with later responses recruited only after earlier ones fail. Their headline quantitative result: the late-stage choice between contraction and detachment 'is consistent with a fair coin toss' (probabilistic, history-dependent decision). They frame this explicitly as a 'behavioral hierarchy' / 'decision-making' and explicitly DISTINGUISH it from habituation or conditioning - it is NOT learning in the technical sense. NOTE: the task prompt cited 'Marshall' as third author and 'S. coeruleus' as the species; the verified third author is Jeremy Gunawardena and the species is S. roeseli. The 'Marshall' association belongs to the SEPARATE 2023 Stentor coeruleus habituation paper.
findings.citation: Joseph P. Dexter, Sudhakaran Prabakaran, Jeremy Gunawardena. 'A Complex Hierarchy of Avoidance Behaviors in a Single-Cell Eukaryote.' Current Biology 29(24):4323-4329.e2 (2019). DOI 10.1016/j.cub.2019.10.059; PMID 31813604.
findings.support: Verified via PubMed (PMID 31813604) and Cell/Current Biology pages. Two prompt-supplied details (third author 'Marshall', species 'coeruleus') were INCORRECT and corrected against the primary source.

findings.item: Stentor 2023 - genuine non-associative LEARNING (habituation) in a single cell
findings.claim: Rajan, Makushok, Kalish et al. (Marshall lab, 2023, Current Biology) demonstrated HABITUATION (non-associative learning) in single Stentor coeruleus cells under calibrated mechanical stimulation, satisfying classical Thompson & Spencer hallmarks: stimulus specificity, frequency/intensity dependence, and spontaneous recovery (after ~15 min pause). Key mechanistic finding: habituation in an individual cell is a single STEP-LIKE binary switch from responsive to non-responsive (modeled as a two-state stochastic machine sensitive to input time-series), NOT a gradual decline; population-level gradation arises from the distribution of switch times across cells. They distinguish this from sensory adaptation/fatigue. This is the cleaner single-cell LEARNING result; the 2019 hierarchy paper is decision-making, not learning. This is the paper genuinely associated with W.F. Marshall.
findings.citation: Deepa Rajan, Tatyana Makushok, Asa Kalish, ..., Mark M. Slabodnick, Wallace F. Marshall. 'Single-cell analysis of habituation in Stentor coeruleus.' Current Biology 33(2):241-251.e4 (2023). DOI 10.1016/j.cub.2022.11.010; PMID 36435177.
findings.support: Verified via PubMed (PMID 36435177) and Cell landing page; full author list and step-like-switch finding confirmed.

findings.item: Physarum maze-solving
findings.claim: Nakagaki, Yamada & Toth (2000, Nature) showed the acellular plasmodium of Physarum polycephalum finds the minimum-length path through a maze between two food sources: in 14 of 19 trials it selected the shortest or second-shortest path (the latter differing by ~2%). Framed as path-optimization / 'primitive intelligence', NOT learning or memory in the conditioning sense.
findings.citation: Toshiyuki Nakagaki, Hiroyasu Yamada, Agota Toth. 'Maze-solving by an amoeboid organism.' Nature 407(6803):470 (2000). DOI 10.1038/35035159; PMID 11028990.
findings.support: Verified via PubMed (PMID 11028990), Nature and ADS records. 14/19 statistic from the published abstract.

findings.item: Physarum habituation + spontaneous recovery (non-associative learning)
findings.claim: Boisseau, Vogel & Dussutour (2016, Proc. R. Soc. B) reported habituation in Physarum polycephalum: when crossing a bridge laced with the harmless bitter repellents quinine or caffeine, plasmodia progressively reduced avoidance over days, then showed spontaneous recovery after ~2 days without the stimulus. They argue it meets habituation criteria and used STIMULUS SPECIFICITY (quinine-habituated plasmodia still avoided caffeine and vice versa) to rule out sensory adaptation / generalized motor fatigue. LOAD-BEARING CAVEAT (authors state it): Physarum is a single cell but MULTINUCLEATE / acellular plasmodium ('unicellular but multi-nucleated eukaryote') - one membrane-bounded cell with many nuclei, which complicates a clean 'single-cell cognition' claim (it is not mononucleate, and the integrating unit is debated).
findings.citation: Romain P. Boisseau, David Vogel, Audrey Dussutour. 'Habituation in non-neural organisms: evidence from slime moulds.' Proceedings of the Royal Society B 283(1829):20160446 (2016). DOI 10.1098/rspb.2016.0446; PMC4855389.
findings.support: Verified via Royal Society landing page and PMC4855389. Multinucleate caveat confirmed in the paper's own language. The exact count of which Thompson-Spencer criteria were formally satisfied is paraphrase from fetched full text, not verbatim.

findings.item: Physarum memory transfer by fusion
findings.claim: Vogel & Dussutour (2016, Proc. R. Soc. B) reported that a salt-habituated Physarum plasmodium can transfer the acquired behaviour to a NAIVE plasmodium simply by fusing with it (>2,000 plasmodia trained). Offered as transfer of a learned state via cytoplasmic fusion. CAVEAT: same multinucleate-cell complication; 'transfer' is cell-cell cytoplasmic fusion, not a packaged memory molecule isolated and re-injected; the mechanism of the transferred state is not identified.
findings.citation: David Vogel, Audrey Dussutour. 'Direct transfer of learned behaviour via cell fusion in non-neural organisms.' Proceedings of the Royal Society B 283(1845):20162382 (2016). DOI 10.1098/rspb.2016.2382; PMID 28003457; PMC5204175.
findings.support: Verified via Royal Society and PubMed (PMID 28003457). Authorship matches the prompt exactly.

findings.item: THE SKEPTICAL POLE - Gershman, Balbi, Gallistel & Gunawardena 2021 (accept vs reject)
findings.claim: Gershman, Balbi, Gallistel & Gunawardena (2021, eLife) ACCEPT that non-associative learning (e.g. habituation) in single cells is real and uncontroversial. Their CONTESTED move is to REHABILITATE associative (Pavlovian) learning in single cells: they re-examine Beatrice Gelber's 1950s Paramecium aurelia conditioning experiments and conclude her experiments 'though not without their limitations, convincingly demonstrated Pavlovian conditioning in Paramecia,' arguing the classic critiques (Jensen's thigmotropism / bacteria-contamination account) deviated methodologically from Gelber's protocol. This is a REINTERPRETATION / argument, NOT new data, and runs against the prevailing consensus. They suggest molecular storage (DNA methylation, histone modification) rather than synaptic plasticity. FOR BALANCE: this paper is itself a contested position - it argues FOR reconsidering but does not settle the question.
findings.citation: Samuel J. Gershman, Petra E.M. Balbi, C. Randy Gallistel, Jeremy Gunawardena. 'Reconsidering the evidence for learning in single cells.' eLife 10:e61907 (2021). DOI 10.7554/eLife.61907; PMID 33395388; PMCID PMC7781593.
findings.support: Verified via eLife and PMC7781593. Direct quote ('convincingly demonstrated Pavlovian conditioning') extracted from full text. Authorship and venue match the prompt exactly.

findings.item: THE SKEPTICAL POLE - Paramecium associative-conditioning claims are contested and largely unreplicated
findings.claim: The historical associative-learning claims in Paramecium are GENUINELY CONTESTED with a poor replication record: (a) Gelber's Pavlovian results (1950s) - Katz & Deterline (1958) FAILED to replicate; Jensen (1957) gave a bacteria/thigmotropism alternative; (b) Hennessey, Rucker & McDiarmid (1979, Animal Learning & Behavior) reported classical conditioning (vibration CS + shock US) in Paramecium caudatum, NEVER independently replicated; (c) Armus, Montgomery & Gurney (2006, Psychological Reports) reported brightness-discrimination learning but the design has a documented light-dark counterbalance confound, with only a PARTIAL later replication (Alipour et al. 2018). NET: as of 2024-2026 the field accepts NON-ASSOCIATIVE single-cell learning (habituation) as real, while ASSOCIATIVE (Pavlovian/operant) single-cell learning remains unsettled with no robust independent replication of the foundational claims. Gershman et al. 2021 is the minority pro-reconsideration position, not consensus.
findings.citation: Hennessey, Rucker & McDiarmid, 'Classical conditioning in paramecia,' Animal Learning & Behavior 7(4):417-423 (1979), DOI 10.3758/BF03209695. Armus, Montgomery & Gurney, 'Discrimination Learning and Extinction in Paramecia (P. caudatum),' Psychological Reports 98(3):705-711 (2006), DOI 10.2466/pr0.98.3.705-711. Gelber controversy / Katz & Deterline 1958 / Jensen 1957 as recounted in Gershman et al. 2021 (PMC7781593).
findings.support: Hennessey 1979 and Armus 2006 verified via Springer/SAGE records. The 'never replicated' / 'methodological artifact' / Katz-Deterline-failed-to-replicate statements are from web summaries and the Gershman review's recounting, NOT independent fetch of Katz&Deterline 1958, Jensen 1957, or Alipour 2018. Confidence MEDIUM on precise replication history; the qualitative 'associative single-cell learning is contested/unreplicated' is HIGH and is the literature's own framing.

findings.item: Cell-intrinsic molecular memory - Walters 2012 (the F253 vertebrate bridge)
findings.claim: Walters (2012, Front. Physiol.) showed the spinal-cord-injury-induced hyperexcitable / spontaneously-active (HSA) state of nociceptors PERSISTS in DISSOCIATED, LOW-DENSITY culture lacking serum or growth factors, 1 day after dissociation and 5+ months after injury - the persistent excitability state is INTRINSIC TO THE INDIVIDUAL CELL, not dependent on circuit or tissue. Walters uses 'cellular memory within nociceptors.' KEY DISTINCTION (do not conflate): this is STATE-PERSISTENCE / hysteresis of a functional state, a DIFFERENT sense from associative/non-associative LEARNING (no stimulus-contingent acquisition of a new response is shown in the dish - it is survival of an already-induced state). Strong evidence for cell-resident, circuit-independent state storage; NOT evidence for single-cell learning per se.
findings.citation: Edgar T. Walters. 'Nociceptors as chronic drivers of pain and hyperreflexia after spinal cord injury: an adaptive-maladaptive hyperfunctional state hypothesis.' Frontiers in Physiology 3:309 (2012). DOI 10.3389/fphys.2012.00309; PMID 22934060; PMCID PMC3429080.
findings.support: Verified via PMC3429080; exact dissociated-low-density-culture quote and 'cellular memory' framing extracted from full text. Matches F253's existing attestation.

findings.item: Cell-intrinsic molecular memory - CPEB prion-like translational state (Si/Kandel lineage + Bogen et al. 2012)
findings.claim: A self-sustaining prion-like translational state is a candidate molecular memory substrate. The Si & Kandel lineage showed neuronal Aplysia CPEB forms self-perpetuating amyloid-like multimers stabilizing long-term synaptic facilitation (prion-like self-templating persistence). Bogen, Alessandri-Haber, Chu, Gear & Levine (2012, J. Neurosci.) extended this to the peripheral nociceptor: PKCepsilon-mediated activation of CPEB generates a long-lasting 'pain memory' (hyperalgesic priming); authors explicitly state 'a self-perpetuating conformer of CPEB constitutes a form of pain memory.' DISTINCTION: like Walters, this is SELF-SUSTAINING STATE PERSISTENCE (bistability via a self-templating molecule), a different sense from learning; it is the molecular MECHANISM by which a cell could hold a state cell-autonomously.
findings.citation: Oliver Bogen, Nicole Alessandri-Haber, Carissa Chu, Robert W. Gear, Jon D. Levine. 'Generation of a Pain Memory in the Primary Afferent Nociceptor Triggered by PKCepsilon Activation of CPEB.' Journal of Neuroscience 32(6):2018-2026 (2012). DOI 10.1523/JNEUROSCI.5138-11.2012. (Si/Kandel CPEB-prion lineage: e.g. Si et al., Cell 140:421-435, 2010, DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2009.12.041, PMID 20144764.)
findings.support: Bogen et al. 2012 verified via J. Neurosci. landing page (full author list, vol/issue/pages, DOI); 'pain memory' / self-perpetuating-conformer framing confirmed. Si et al. 2010 verified at PubMed/search level (PMID 20144764) as representative of the lineage the prompt named generically as 'Si/Kandel'.

findings.item: Brain = scaled compute-organelle / origin-of-neurons reading
findings.claim: There IS substantial literature treating the neuron as a cell that SPECIALIZED an ancestral, cell-general signalling/secretory capacity, supporting 'synaptic genes predate synapses': (a) Arendt et al. (2016, Nat. Rev. Genet.) 'sister cell type' framework - neurons and other cell types descend from shared precursors via divergence of a core regulatory complex; (b) Burkhardt & Sprecher (2017, BioEssays) - neurons, sponge globular cells, and placozoan gland cells may share a primordial secretory/sensory cell ancestor; homologs of key neuronal/synaptic proteins are expressed in neuron-less sponges, placozoans, and unicellular choanoflagellates; (c) Moroz et al. (2014, Nature) - ctenophore genome supports INDEPENDENT (convergent) origin of neural systems, implying the underlying excitable/signalling toolkit is ancestral and repeatedly co-opted. CAVEAT: these support 'neurons specialize an ancestral cell-general toolkit' but do NOT make the framework's 'brain : organism :: compute-organelle : cell' claim; that mapping is framework-reading, not their assertion. (Penrose-Hameroff quantum-microtubule consciousness is fringe/contested and did NOT surface in the verified primary literature; flagged out-of-scope.)
findings.citation: Arendt et al., 'The origin and evolution of cell types.' Nature Reviews Genetics 17(12):744-757 (2016), DOI 10.1038/nrg.2016.127, PMID 27818507. Burkhardt & Sprecher, 'Evolutionary origin of synapses and neurons - Bridging the gap,' BioEssays 39(10):1700024 (2017), DOI 10.1002/bies.201700024. Moroz et al., 'The ctenophore genome and the evolutionary origins of neural systems,' Nature 510(7503):109-114 (2014), DOI 10.1038/nature13400, PMID 24847885.
findings.support: All three verified: Arendt 2016 (PMID 27818507, full author list); Burkhardt & Sprecher 2017 (Wiley/BioEssays page); Moroz 2014 (PMID 24847885, Nature 510:109-114). 'Synaptic genes predate synapses' is the literature's own; the 'compute-organelle' mapping is explicitly flagged as framework-reading.

opus_survey.cross_cutting:
EVIDENCE RANKING on the F254 axis (cell-autonomous compute vs compute-requires-multicellularity), strongest-to-weakest support for CELL-AUTONOMY, both poles held:

TIER 1 - CLEANLY supports cell-autonomous compute/decision/state:
- Stentor 2019 (Dexter/Prabakaran/Gunawardena): a genuine SEQUENTIAL DECISION HIERARCHY with a probabilistic ('fair coin toss') terminal choice, in a MONONUCLEATE single cell. Decision-making, not learning - but cleanly cell-autonomous and well-controlled.
- Stentor 2023 (Rajan/Marshall): genuine NON-ASSOCIATIVE LEARNING (habituation; step-like switch; spontaneous recovery; stimulus-specific) in a MONONUCLEATE single cell. Strongest single-cell LEARNING datum because habituation is the accepted-as-real category AND it is a true single cell.
- Walters 2012 + Bogen 2012/CPEB: cell-INTRINSIC state persistence in dissociated mammalian neurons - strongest VERTEBRATE anchor that a learned-state-like trace is held inside one cell. But this is STATE-PERSISTENCE/hysteresis, a DIFFERENT sense from learning (no acquisition demonstrated in the dish).

TIER 2 - supports cell-autonomy WITH a load-bearing caveat:
- Physarum maze-solving / habituation / fusion-transfer (Nakagaki 2000; Boisseau 2016; Vogel & Dussutour 2016): striking, but Physarum is MULTINUCLEATE (acellular plasmodium) - single-cell by membrane, not by genome-copy - so a contested exemplar of 'single-CELL' cognition.

TIER 3 - CONTESTED / does NOT cleanly support (skeptical pole at full strength):
- Associative/Pavlovian single-cell learning (Gelber; Hennessey 1979; Armus 2006): foundational claims largely UNREPLICATED (Katz & Deterline failed to replicate Gelber; Hennessey never replicated; Armus has a counterbalance confound). Gershman et al. 2021 argues FOR reconsidering, but that is a minority reinterpretation, not a settled result. Field consensus 2024-2026: non-associative single-cell learning = real; associative single-cell learning = unsettled/contested.

WHERE THE LITERATURE LANDS ON F254's FALSIFIER (F-a, 'compute genuinely REQUIRES multicellularity'): The verified literature does NOT supply any result showing learning/decision is IMPOSSIBLE in a single cell - the opposite holds for non-associative learning and decision hierarchies (Stentor) and for cell-intrinsic state persistence (Walters/CPEB). So on the narrow falsifier as stated, current evidence does NOT falsify F254 and leans toward cell-autonomy FOR non-associative learning, decision-making, and state-persistence. HOWEVER (honest counter-pressure): this only covers the WEAKER senses of 'compute.' The STRONGER sense (associative/predictive learning) is exactly where single-cell evidence is contested-to-absent. If F254's 'compute' is meant to include associative/predictive learning, the literature is SILENT-to-NEGATIVE at the single-cell level - the live risk to the conjecture. The origin-of-neurons literature (Arendt/Burkhardt/Moroz) is consistent with 'neurons specialize an ancestral cell-general toolkit' but makes NO claim about a within-cell 'compute-organelle' and does not on its own support the scale-recursive 'brain:organism::compute-organelle:cell' mapping - that is framework-reading only.
opus_survey.uncentered_note: I did not lean toward the framework's preferred (cell-autonomous) answer. The skeptical pole is reported at full strength and, on the strongest sense of 'compute' (associative/predictive learning), is the WINNING reading at the single-cell level: the foundational Paramecium associative-conditioning claims (Gelber, Hennessey, Armus) are unreplicated or confounded, and Gershman et al. 2021 - though it argues for reconsideration - is itself a contested minority position, not vindication. Genuine state of the field: non-associative learning (habituation) and decision hierarchies in single cells are REAL and well-supported (Stentor 2019/2023); associative learning in single cells is NOT established. Two distinct senses of 'memory' were kept separate and NOT conflated: (1) LEARNING (stimulus-contingent acquisition - Stentor habituation, contested Paramecium conditioning) vs (2) STATE-PERSISTENCE / hysteresis (Walters HSA, CPEB prion-like self-templating) - the latter is cell-autonomous and strong but is NOT learning. For non-leaning balance: a result that WOULD strongly support F254 cell-autonomy (clean associative learning in a true mononucleate single cell) does not currently exist; the strongest cell-autonomous evidence is for the weaker senses (decision, habituation, state-persistence). I did NOT center the framework's compute-organelle mapping: the origin-of-neurons literature is offered as a LENS the cited authors do not make. Two prompt-supplied citation details were wrong and I corrected rather than echoed them: Stentor 2019's third author is Gunawardena not Marshall, and the species is S. roeseli not S. coeruleus; the 'Marshall' + 'S. coeruleus' pairing belongs to the separate 2023 habituation paper.
gaps: Did NOT fetch primary texts of the historical skeptical sources: Jensen 1957 (Behaviour), Katz & Deterline 1958, Alipour et al. 2018 partial replication. The replication-failure chain is from web summaries and Gershman et al. 2021's recounting, not independent primary verification. Confidence on the precise replication history is MEDIUM; the qualitative 'associative single-cell learning is contested' is HIGH.

Did NOT independently fetch Si et al. 2010 (Cell) full text; the CPEB-prion lineage is verified at PubMed/search level (PMID 20144764) and via Bogen 2012's framing, not by primary full-text extraction.

The exact enumeration of WHICH Thompson & Spencer 1966 habituation criteria each Physarum/Stentor paper formally satisfied is paraphrased from fetched full text and secondary summary; treat the specific criteria lists as paraphrase, not verbatim. Thompson & Spencer 1966 itself was not fetched.

Did NOT resolve the deeper conceptual question the multinucleate caveat raises: whether the integrating 'decision' unit in Physarum is the cell, the syncytium, or an emergent network of nuclei/oscillators - the literature is genuinely unsettled here and it is reported as an open caveat, not resolved.

F254's falsifier as written ('compute genuinely requiring multicellularity') is only cleanly addressable for non-associative/decision/state senses of 'compute.' For the strong (associative/predictive) sense the literature is contested-to-silent at the single-cell level, so F254 is neither confirmed nor falsified on its hardest interpretation - a genuine gap, not a verdict.

Penrose-Hameroff quantum-microtubule-consciousness did not surface in the verified primary literature; flagged as fringe/out-of-scope per instructions but not affirmatively searched-and-refuted (by design).

findings.item: Stentor roeseli — behavioral hierarchy (Dexter, Prabakaran & Gunawardena 2019)
findings.claim: Dexter et al. confirmed, using video microscopy and calibrated micro-flow irritant delivery, that S. roeseli exhibits a statistically non-random sequential hierarchy of avoidance behaviors: (1) bending/ciliary alteration attempted first; (2) contraction; (3) detachment — in that fixed partial order. Detachment never occurred without prior contraction. The choice between contraction and detachment approximated a fair coin toss (~50/50). The authors replicated Jennings 1906 and refuted the earlier 1967 non-replication, which had used the wrong species (S. coeruleus instead of S. roeseli). IMPORTANT PRECISION: The authors explicitly framed this as 'sequential decision-making,' NOT learning in the technical sense. They stated their findings 'demonstrate that the organism's decision making is distinct from habituation or classical conditioning.' Gunawardena acknowledged no known mechanism explains how a single cell implements this hierarchy. The paper's claim is behavioral hierarchy / graded sequential responding under repeated stimulation — not associative or non-associative learning by the Thompson-Spencer criteria.
findings.citation: Dexter JP, Prabakaran S, Gunawardena J. 'A Complex Hierarchy of Avoidance Behaviors in a Single-Cell Eukaryote.' Current Biology 29(24):4323-4329.e2, December 2019. DOI: 10.1016/j.cub.2019.10.059. PMID: 31813604. OA via Cell.com extended PDF. VERIFIED: title, authors, journal, year, DOI confirmed across multiple sources.
findings.support: Confirmed via multiple independent web sources including PubMed, Cell.com, EurekAlert, Dartmouth press release, and SciTechDaily. Species clarification (roeseli not coeruleus) confirmed via Gershman et al. 2021 PMC text and direct search.

findings.item: Stentor coeruleus — habituation study (Rajan et al. 2022)
findings.claim: A separate 2022 Current Biology study (not Dexter; different species: S. coeruleus) by Rajan et al. demonstrated habituation in single cells using calibrated mechanical stimuli. Key quantitative results: contraction probability declined from ~95% at stimulus 1 to ~20-30% by stimulus 30 (high force, 1-min intervals). At individual cell level, 20/22 cells showed statistically significant step-like switching between responsive and non-responsive states (p<0.02). After 15 minutes rest, 90% of habituated cells recovered responsiveness (forgetting rate ~0.15/min, ~150-fold higher than habituation rate ~0.001/min). Controls excluded mechanical exhaustion (strong stimuli still elicited contraction in habituated cells; repeated strong stimuli prevented habituation) and local receptor adaptation (stimulation of one region produced whole-cell habituation). Recovery after rest, stimulus specificity, and force-dependence meet Thompson-Spencer criteria for habituation as opposed to sensory adaptation or motor fatigue. Authors explicitly claimed this as 'habituation' (a form of non-associative learning), not mere adaptation. NOTE: This is S. coeruleus, distinct from the Dexter 2019 S. roeseli paper.
findings.citation: Rajan R et al. 'Single-cell analysis of habituation in Stentor coeruleus.' Current Biology 32(24), November 2022. DOI: 10.1016/j.cub.2022.11.048. PMID: 36435177. OA: PMC9877177. VERIFIED: title, authors, journal, year, DOI confirmed.
findings.support: PMC full text fetched directly (PMC9877177) with quantitative detail extracted. Step-switch model, statistics, and controls all recovered from primary source.

findings.item: Physarum polycephalum — maze-solving (Nakagaki, Yamada & Toth 2000)
findings.claim: Physarum plasmodium placed in a maze with food at two endpoints reorganized its tubular network to find the shortest (or second-shortest) path in ~8 hours. In 14/19 trials, the shortest or near-shortest path was selected (paths differing by ~2% in length). Mechanism: selective tube remodeling — tubes in dead-end paths shrink while the path connecting food sources is reinforced. This is NOT learning by any standard definition: it is an optimization via physically embodied network dynamics (the organism's body literally reshapes to minimize path length through iterative contraction/reinforcement of tubes). The authors themselves used the word 'intelligence' loosely in the Nature letter title, but the mechanism is more accurately described as analog network optimization, not symbolic or associative learning. CRITICAL CAVEAT: Physarum is a multinucleate acellular plasmodium — a single cell containing thousands of nuclei with no cell membranes between them (syncytium). Whether this counts as 'single-cell' cognition is contested (see finding 5).
findings.citation: Nakagaki T, Yamada H, Toth A. 'Maze-solving by an amoeboid organism.' Nature 407(6803):470, September 2000. DOI: 10.1038/35035159. PMID: 11028990. OA abstract via Nature/PubMed. VERIFIED: authors, title, journal, year, DOI confirmed.
findings.support: Confirmed across Nature, PubMed, ADS, and RepEc. Mechanism detail (tube remodeling, 14/19 trials) from published abstract and summary sources.

findings.item: Physarum polycephalum — habituation (Boisseau, Vogel & Dussutour 2016)
findings.claim: Over 9 days, three groups of Physarum plasmodia crossed bridges treated with quinine, caffeine, or nothing (control) to reach food. Quinine/caffeine groups initially avoided the repellent bridge but by day 6 crossed at the same speed as controls (habituation = response decline). Spontaneous recovery occurred after stimulus withdrawal. Critically, quinine-habituated animals did not reduce aversion to caffeine, and vice versa (stimulus specificity). These three criteria — response decrement, spontaneous recovery, stimulus specificity — meet Thompson-Spencer (1966) criteria for habituation as distinct from sensory adaptation or motor fatigue. The Boisseau et al. authors explicitly claimed this as 'habituation, an unmistakable form of learning.' CAVEAT: Gershman et al. (2021) do NOT extensively critique the Physarum work in their eLife paper, which focuses primarily on Paramecium associative learning. The habituation result has not been prominently non-replicated in the literature retrieved, but independent replication data were not identified in this search. MULTINUCLEATE CAVEAT: see finding 5.
findings.citation: Boisseau RP, Vogel D, Dussutour A. 'Habituation in non-neural organisms: evidence from slime moulds.' Proceedings of the Royal Society B 283(1829):20160446, April 2016. DOI: 10.1098/rspb.2016.0446. OA: Royal Society Publishing. VERIFIED: authors, title, journal, year, DOI confirmed.
findings.support: Multiple independent confirmations including Royal Society, ResearchGate, Dryad data repository. Stimulus-specificity and spontaneous recovery confirmed across multiple summary sources.

findings.item: Physarum — memory transfer by cell fusion (Vogel & Dussutour 2016)
findings.claim: Habituated Physarum plasmodia (trained to cross quinine bridge) were fused with naive unhabituated plasmodia. The fused organism crossed the quinine bridge faster than naive controls, suggesting the habituated state was transferred through cytoplasmic mixing. Authors described this as 'direct transfer of learned behaviour via cell fusion.' This is a striking result with no direct parallel in neural organisms, but several caveats apply: (a) the mechanism is unknown — it could be transfer of a specific molecular state (e.g., a small molecule, phosphorylation state, or gene expression change) rather than 'memory' in any representational sense; (b) MULTINUCLEATE CAVEAT applies (see finding 5); (c) this paper has not been prominently non-replicated in retrieved sources but independent confirmation was not identified.
findings.citation: Vogel D, Dussutour A. 'Direct transfer of learned behaviour via cell fusion in non-neural organisms.' Proceedings of the Royal Society B 283(1845):20162382, December 2016. DOI: 10.1098/rspb.2016.2382. PMID: 28003457. OA: PMC5204175. VERIFIED: authors, title, journal, year, DOI confirmed.
findings.support: Confirmed across PubMed, PMC, ResearchGate, phys.org. Paper venue is Proc R Soc B, not Current Biology as originally stated in task prompt — corrected here.

findings.item: CRITICAL CAVEAT: Is Physarum a 'single cell'?
findings.claim: Physarum polycephalum in plasmodial form is a SYNCYTIUM: a single continuous cytoplasm containing thousands to millions of nuclei, with NO cell membranes separating nuclei. It arises from the fusion of haploid amoebae that undergo mitotic nuclear division without cytokinesis. It is technically ONE cell by the absence-of-membranes criterion, but it contains the genomic complement of a multicellular organism distributed across one cytoplasm. This is a LOAD-BEARING complication for any claim of 'single-cell cognition': (a) information integration may occur between nuclei communicating via shared cytoplasm, which is qualitatively different from information processing within a mononucleate cell; (b) the spatial scale of a mature plasmodium can reach tens of centimeters, far beyond typical single-cell size; (c) critics (e.g., noted in Gershman et al. context) can argue Physarum habituation reflects network-level dynamics of a distributed cytoplasmic syncytium rather than cell-intrinsic computation. Proponents counter that the single shared cytoplasm IS the relevant unit. The debate is genuine and not fully resolved in the literature.
findings.citation: Wikipedia article on Physarum polycephalum (structural description); MicrobeWiki Kenyon entry; Moroz LL 'Multiple Origins of Neurons From Secretory Cells' Frontiers Cell Dev Biol 2021 (syncytial biology context). Structural biology of syncytia: standard cell biology texts. FLAG: No single definitive primary source attest this specific controversy — it is distributed across multiple sources.
findings.support: Syncytial/multinucleate nature of Physarum plasmodium is uncontested cell biology. The complication for 'single-cell cognition' claims is widely noted in review literature (Thoughts from the Forest Floor, Animal Cognition 2023, PMC10770251).

findings.item: THE SKEPTICAL POLE: Gershman, Balbi, Gallistel & Gunawardena 2021 (eLife)
findings.claim: This paper is a REHABILITATION of single-cell learning claims, not a skeptical critique — but it is careful about what it accepts. WHAT IT ACCEPTS: (1) Non-associative learning (habituation) in single cells is accepted as established. (2) Stentor roeseli behavioral hierarchy is accepted as genuine (the Dexter 2019 vindication). (3) Gelber's (1952/1958) Paramecium Pavlovian conditioning experiments are re-evaluated as potentially genuine evidence that was unjustly dismissed. WHAT THE HISTORICAL SKEPTICS SAID (and what Gershman et al. rebut): Donald Jensen argued Gelber's increased wire-attachment results reflected thigmotropism (haptic attraction) via residual bacteria around the wire, not conditioning. Katz & Deterline's 'stirring' control appeared to eliminate learning. Gershman et al. reinterpret the stirring result as 'contingency degradation' (decorrelation of CS and US), which is known to suppress conditioning in any learning system — making the stirring experiment consistent with, not refuting, genuine conditioning. Armus et al. (2006) Paramecium conditioning claims were identified as potentially artifactual (improper counterbalance of light-dark conditions). Hennessey et al. (1979) used proper Rescorla random-control; their results survive the review more intact. OVERALL STATUS as of 2021: The paper argues the non-replication history reflects (a) species substitution errors (Stentor), (b) contingency-degradation misinterpretation (Paramecium), and (c) methodological artifacts — not genuine absence of learning. The associative-learning evidence for single cells remains CONTESTED and not confirmed by independent replication; Gershman et al. argue the case for reconsidering it, not that it is established.
findings.citation: Gershman SJ, Balbi PE, Gallistel CR, Gunawardena J. 'Reconsidering the evidence for learning in single cells.' eLife 10:e61907, 2021. DOI: 10.7554/eLife.61907. PMID: 33395388. OA: PMC7781593. VERIFIED: authors, title, journal, year, DOI confirmed via eLife and PMC full text.
findings.support: PMC full text fetched (PMC7781593) and eLife page fetched directly. Key arguments extracted from primary source. Paper is OA.

findings.item: Historical non-replications: Paramecium conditioning (Hennessey, Armus lineage)
findings.claim: Beatrice Gelber (1952, 1958) reported Pavlovian conditioning in Paramecium aurelia. Donald Jensen (1957) argued the results reflected bacterial contamination/thigmotropism and was NOT properly controlled. Hennessey et al. (1979) used vibration CS + shock US with Rescorla random controls in Paramecium caudatum — their results have been cited as positive but NEVER INDEPENDENTLY REPLICATED (per Gershman et al. 2021 review and general literature summary). Armus et al. (2006) reported Paramecium conditioning but the counterbalancing analysis was identified as flawed (light-dark confound not properly controlled). Trial-and-error learning replication by French (1940) and Mirsky & Katz was mixed. The field status as of 2024-2026: associative learning in Paramecium and other protists remains UNCONFIRMED BY ROBUST INDEPENDENT REPLICATION. The non-associative learning (habituation in Stentor, Physarum) is on firmer ground by Thompson-Spencer criteria, but the stronger claim of associative/Pavlovian conditioning lacks confirmed replication.
findings.citation: Gershman et al. eLife 2021 (as above); Hennessey TM et al. (1979) cited within Gershman et al.; Armus HL et al. (2006) 'Discrimination Learning in Paramecia,' Psychological Record, identified as potentially artifactual in Gershman review. FLAG: Hennessey 1979 original paper not independently verified at source — reported through Gershman et al. secondary account.

Treat as: established that these studies exist and that Gershman et al. discuss them; specific methodological critiques are Gershman et al.'s reading, not independently verified here.

findings.item: Walters 2012 — nociceptor intrinsic hyperfunctional state (Front. Physiol.)
findings.claim: Walters (2012) proposed that spinal cord injury triggers a persistent 'hyperspontaneous activity' (HSA) state in nociceptors that (a) persists in vivo for months to years post-SCI, and (b) is expressed 1 day after dissociation in LOW-DENSITY CULTURE lacking serum or growth factors, at an incidence of 35-70% 3 days to 8+ months post-SCI. The critical claim for F254: the HSA state is INTRINSIC — Walters explicitly states 'the intrinsic HSA state is persistent' and that it does not require ongoing central or peripheral circuit inputs. Walters frames this as a 'nociceptor memory' and invokes 'hyperalgesic priming' as an example where a single acute inflammation episode produces lasting sensitivity days/weeks later. This is a HYPOTHESIS AND THEORY article (not a primary experimental report); the experimental support cited is drawn from Bedi et al. and other Walters lab papers on Aplysia nociceptors and rat DRG. FLAG: the 2012 paper is explicitly a hypothesis paper, not a primary data paper.
findings.citation: Walters ET. 'Nociceptors as chronic drivers of pain and hyperreflexia after spinal cord injury: an adaptive-maladaptive hyperfunctional state hypothesis.' Frontiers in Physiology 3:309, August 2012. DOI: 10.3389/fphys.2012.00309. PMID: UNVERIFIED. OA: Frontiers, PMC3429080. VERIFIED: authors, title, journal, year, DOI confirmed via Frontiers and PMC.
findings.support: PMC full text fetched (PMC3429080). Intrinsic-state and dissociated-culture claim extracted from primary source text. PMID not retrieved but DOI confirmed.

findings.item: Bavencoffe, Zhu, Walters et al. 2024 — cAMP-induced long-term hyperexcitability in ISOLATED nociceptors
findings.claim: This 2024 bioRxiv/PMC paper directly tests intrinsic cellular memory in dissociated DRG nociceptors from naive (uninjured) rats. Six-hour treatment with prucalopride (5-HT4 agonist, 1 uM) or forskolin (adenylyl cyclase activator) induced long-term hyperexcitability (LTH) persisting 12-24 hours after washout, in isolated cells with no circuit connections. Ongoing activity at subthreshold membrane potential (-45 mV): vehicle 0-8% of cells; prucalopride 37-50% of cells (Fisher's exact, p<0.05). Resting membrane potential depolarized from -69 to -66 mV (p<0.05). PKA inhibitor, CREB inhibitor, transcription inhibitor, and protein-synthesis inhibitor all abolished LTH (p<0.025–0.0005 Bonferroni-corrected, 17 experiments). Authors explicitly connect this to 'memory-related' mechanisms: 'a prototypical cellular signaling pathway previously found to induce memory-related synaptic LTP.' IMPORTANT DISTINCTION: this is STATE PERSISTENCE induced by a specific pharmacological trigger in isolated cells — it is 'cellular memory' in the hysteresis/state-persistence sense, not learning (no CS-US pairing, no modification of future responding based on experience of contingencies). The authors use 'memory-like aftereffect' language, not 'learning.'
findings.citation: Bavencoffe A, Zhu MY, Neerukonda SV, Johnson KN, Dessauer CW, Walters ET. 'Induction of long-term hyperexcitability by memory-related cAMP signaling in isolated nociceptor cell bodies.' bioRxiv 2024.07.13.603393 (preprint); published PMC11470187. DOI: 10.1101/2024.07.13.603393. OA: PMC11470187. VERIFIED: authors, title, venue, year, DOI confirmed via bioRxiv and PMC.
findings.support: PMC full text fetched (PMC11470187). All quantitative claims extracted directly from primary source. This is a preprint also available in PMC — peer-review status not fully confirmed.

findings.item: CPEB / prion-like synaptic memory — Si, Lindquist & Kandel (2003) + Fioriti et al. (2015)
findings.claim: Si et al. (2003, Cell) identified a neuronal isoform of Aplysia CPEB (cytoplasmic polyadenylation element-binding protein) with prion-like properties: it can self-perpetuate in an active (aggregated) conformation at stimulated synapses, activating dormant mRNAs to maintain synapse-specific long-term facilitation. This is a single-synapse-level molecular state-persistence mechanism — a specific synapse can be 'marked' by CPEB aggregation and maintain elevated local translation. Fioriti et al. (2015, Neuron) extended this to mouse CPEB3: genetic ablation of CPEB3 impairs maintenance of hippocampal LTP and hippocampus-dependent spatial memory. Bogen & Levine reference in task prompt: search did not find a 2012 Bogen & Levine paper on CPEB — possible citation error in task prompt (the major 2012 work on CPEB activation is 'Neuralized1 activates CPEB3,' Neuron, PMID: 22153079, by Pavlopoulos et al.). FLAG: 'Bogen & Levine 2012' as cited in the task was NOT FOUND — could not verify. IMPORTANT DISTINCTION: CPEB prion-like mechanism is state persistence at the synapse level within a neuron — it is a WITHIN-CELL memory mechanism. Whether this constitutes 'computation' in the sense of decision-making is a further inferential step the literature does not directly make.

PMID: 14697205. VERIFIED: authors, title, journal, year confirmed. | Fioriti L et al. 'The Persistence of Hippocampal-Based Memory Requires Protein Synthesis Mediated by the Prion-like Protein CPEB3.' Neuron 86(6):1433-1448, June 2015. PMID: 26074003. VERIFIED. | FLAG: 'Bogen & Levine 2012' NOT FOUND — possible prompt citation error.

findings.item: Single-cell epigenetic/transcriptional memory and bet-hedging
findings.claim: Single cells can maintain heritable transcriptional states through (a) bistable gene-regulatory circuits with feedback, (b) chromatin modification (histone marks, DNA methylation) propagated through mitosis, and (c) stochastic state-switching (bet-hedging). These mechanisms allow a single cell to 'remember' a prior environmental exposure — e.g., a previously activated gene is reactivated faster upon re-exposure (transcriptional memory, established in yeast and mammalian cells). Establishment and Inheritance of Epigenetic Transcriptional Memory (PMC9479176, 2022) reviews this as accelerating reactivation via chromatin changes + poised Pol II. These are STATE-PERSISTENCE mechanisms, not learning: they do not involve modification of future responses to contingently related stimuli. They establish that cell-intrinsic molecular memory (in the hysteresis sense) is real and widespread, but they do not demonstrate computation in the sense of decision-making or associative learning. They ARE directly relevant to the F254 'build+compute fused' framing as evidence that information-state persistence is a basal, universal cellular capacity.

PMC9479176, 2022 (specific journal/DOI not retrieved — FLAG: confirm full citation before lodging). General mechanism: Kaufmann BB, van Oudenaarden A. 'Stochastic gene expression: from single molecules to the proteome.' Current Opinion Cell Biology, and standard epigenetics texts. findings.support: General framework well-established; specific primary citations not all verified at DOI level in this search. Treat as established mechanism but verify individual citations before lodging as AMSC entries.

findings.item: Origin of neurons from secretory/ciliated cells — Burkhardt 2015; Burkhardt & Sprecher 2017; Moroz 2021
findings.claim: Three converging lines of evidence support the 'brain = scaled ancestral compute-organelle' reading: (1) Burkhardt (J Exp Biol 2015): choanoflagellates (closest unicellular relatives of animals) possess diverse synaptic protein homologs, including a primordial neurosecretory apparatus. The mechanism by which presynaptic proteins interact is conserved between choanoflagellates and metazoans. Most synaptic proteins evolved BEFORE neurons existed — they are ancestrally pleiotropic. (2) Burkhardt & Sprecher (BioEssays 2017): non-bilaterian metazoans (animals with and without neurons) and their closest unicellular relatives already contain molecular toolkits for synapse functions. The paper explicitly asks whether neurons evolved once or multiple times. (3) Moroz (Front. Cell Dev. Biol. 2021): neurons evolved MULTIPLE TIMES from genetically distinct secretory cells (polygeny hypothesis, originally from Sakharov 1970s). Early metazoans integrated behavior via non-synaptic volume/paracrine secretion before synapses existed. Ctenophores have a second independent nervous system; diversity of transmitters/receptors predated neural systems. Arendt's sister-cell model (cited in Moroz): novel neuronal cell types arise in pairs via subspecialization of ancestral cell types. These papers directly support: the ancestral signaling/secretory cell had a general-purpose information-processing capacity that neurons SPECIALIZED, not invented from scratch.
findings.citation: Burkhardt P. 'The origin and evolution of synaptic proteins — choanoflagellates lead the way.' J Exp Biol 218(4):506-514, 2015. DOI: 10.1242/jeb.110247. PMID: 25696814. VERIFIED. | Burkhardt P, Sprecher SG. 'Evolutionary origin of synapses and neurons — Bridging the gap.' BioEssays 39(10):1700024, 2017. DOI: 10.1002/bies.201700024. PMID: 28863228. VERIFIED. | Moroz LL. 'Multiple Origins of Neurons From Secretory Cells.' Front Cell Dev Biol 9:669087, 2021. DOI: 10.3389/fcell.2021.669087. PMID: 34307354. OA: PMC8293673. VERIFIED.
findings.support: All three papers confirmed via PubMed, journal sites, and PMC full text (Moroz). DOIs confirmed. Arendt's sister-cell model cited within Moroz PMC text — Arendt primary papers not independently fetched but widely cited.

findings.item: Moroz 2016 — independent evolution of ctenophore nervous system
findings.claim: Moroz et al. (Phil Trans R Soc B 2016; earlier versions 2015) argue that ctenophores evolved a nervous system INDEPENDENTLY from cnidarian/bilaterian neurons: (a) ctenophore neuropeptide homologs are found in no other animal phylum; (b) known bilaterian neuronal markers and many transcription factors are either absent in ctenophores or not expressed in neurons; (c) genomics and metabolomics support polygenesis — neural signaling evolved independently at least twice in animals. This has a direct implication for F254: if neurons can evolve de novo from non-neural secretory cells multiple times, the ancestral capacity (secretory signaling, excitability, vesicle release) must be present in non-neural cells — supporting cell-autonomous computational capacity as ancestral, with neurons as derived specializations.
findings.citation: Moroz LL. 'Independent origins of neurons and synapses: insights from ctenophores.' Phil Trans R Soc B 371(1685):20150041, 2016. DOI: 10.1098/rstb.2015.0041. PMID: 26598724. OA: PMC4685580. VERIFIED: authors, title, journal, year, DOI confirmed.
findings.support: Confirmed via PubMed, Phil Trans R Soc B, PMC. Multiple independent sources.

sonnet_survey.cross_cutting:
SYNTHESIS — RANKING EVIDENCE BY CELL-AUTONOMY vs. CIRCUIT-REQUIREMENT AXIS

The evidence divides into three tiers by how cleanly it maps onto 'compute is cell-autonomous':

TIER 1 — STRONGEST CELL-AUTONOMY EVIDENCE (compute clearly intrinsic to single cell):

(A) Stentor coeruleus habituation (Rajan et al. 2022): 20/22 cells showed statistically significant step-like switching between responsive and non-responsive states driven by stimulus history alone, with no circuit. Recovery kinematics (90% recover in 15 min; 150-fold rate asymmetry between habituation and forgetting) are consistent with a two-state intracellular molecular switch. Controls ruled out fatigue and local adaptation. This is the cleanest single-cell non-associative learning result.

(B) Bavencoffe/Walters 2024 isolated nociceptors: cAMP → PKA → CREB → protein synthesis cascade induces 12-24 hour lasting hyperexcitability in dissociated cells with no synaptic input (0-8% baseline vs. 37-50% treated; p<0.05). The pathway requires gene transcription and protein synthesis — classical memory consolidation hallmarks — in a single isolated cell. This demonstrates cell-autonomous state-persistence via known memory molecular machinery.

(C) CPEB/prion-like self-perpetuating state (Si/Kandel 2003; Fioriti et al. 2015): Synapse-specific molecular state persistence via prion-like CPEB aggregation. This is not 'learning' (no CS-US contingency) but it IS cell-intrinsic state persistence using molecular machinery shared with memory consolidation. Localized to individual synapses within neurons.

TIER 2 — REAL BUT CARRYING CAVEATS (the Physarum cluster):

(D) Physarum habituation (Boisseau et al. 2016): Meets Thompson-Spencer criteria (response decrement, spontaneous recovery, stimulus specificity) but: (i) Physarum is a multinucleate syncytium spanning cm-scale, not a mononucleate cell; (ii) the cognitive unit may be the cytoplasmic network (emergent from thousands of nuclei), not a 'single cell' in the usual sense; (iii) no independent replication identified in this search. Best described as: 'a non-neural acellular organism meets operational criteria for habituation; cell-autonomy is complicated by the syncytial structure.'

(E) Physarum maze-solving (Nakagaki et al. 2000): Not learning; it is physical network optimization via tube remodeling. Relevant as evidence that distributed information processing (optimal path selection) can arise from subcellular dynamics without a nervous system, but it does not constitute learning by any definition.

(F) Physarum memory transfer (Vogel & Dussutour 2016): Striking but mechanistically unexplained. Transfer of habituated state through cytoplasmic fusion is real if the result replicates, but no mechanism was proposed and the syncytial caveat applies.

TIER 3 — BEHAVIORAL HIERARCHY (NOT LEARNING, BUT REAL):

(G) Stentor roeseli decision hierarchy (Dexter et al. 2019): Confirmed genuine sequential avoidance hierarchy in a single mononucleate cell. NOT learning — authors explicitly said so. It demonstrates that a single cell can implement graded priority-ordered responding, which requires something like internal state tracking (the cell 'knows' it has tried behavior N before escalating to N+1), but the mechanism is unknown and not framed as learning.

THE SKEPTICAL POLE AT FULL WEIGHT:

The skeptical case must be stated plainly: (1) Associative/Pavlovian conditioning in single cells (the stronger claim) is NOT established by independent replication. Gershman et al. 2021 argue for reconsidering, not confirming, the Gelber-Hennessey lineage. (2) All non-associative learning (habituation) evidence is contested at the level of alternative mechanism: the molecular pathway producing the behavioral decrement in Physarum is UNKNOWN, so fatigue/metabolic alternatives cannot be fully excluded despite stimulus-specificity controls. (3) Stentor habituation (Rajan 2022) is the strongest non-associative result but is also recent and awaits further independent replication. (4) The question 'does this constitute learning?' depends critically on how the term is operationalized; using the strictest Thompson-Spencer criteria, Stentor coeruleus habituation comes closest to meeting them, but critics could argue the two-state step-switch model is a thermodynamic state-transition, not 'learning' in the cognitive sense. (5) None of the single-cell results involve modification of behavior through contingency learning (CS-US association) with confirmed independent replication.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY F254 (compute requires multicellularity):
The strong falsifier of F254 would be: a finding that (a) a behavioral capability clearly requiring computation (e.g., associative conditioning) cannot be demonstrated in ANY isolated single cell even under ideal conditions, AND (b) that same capability emerges reliably only when cells are in circuits. Current evidence does not provide this falsifier. The habituation and state-persistence results cut the other way. The strongest potential falsifier would be if all apparent single-cell 'learning' results prove to be artifacts (fatigue, metabolic, or syncytial-network effects) under rigorous controls — which the skeptical literature notes is plausible but not established.

WHAT SUPPORTS F254:
(a) Cell-intrinsic state persistence using memory-consolidation molecular machinery (cAMP/PKA/CREB/protein synthesis) in isolated nociceptors — Bavencoffe/Walters 2024. (b) Habituation in S. coeruleus (Rajan 2022). (c) Pre-neural evolutionary history: synaptic genes predate synapses (Burkhardt 2015); neurons evolved multiple times from ancestral secretory cells (Moroz 2021) — implying the ancestral capacity was already there. (d) CPEB prion-like synapse-level state persistence (Si/Kandel 2003).

FRAMEWORK LENS (offered, not asserted — authors cited make no F254 claim):
Reading the F254 conjecture against this literature: 'build+compute fused and cell-resident, brain = scaled compute-organelle' is consistent with (but not proven by) the evolutionary-neuroscience literature. The Burkhardt-Moroz line specifically supports the reading that neurons SPECIALIZED an ancestral secretory-cell capacity rather than invented computation. Whether that ancestral capacity was 'full computation' or only its precursors is a question the current evidence cannot close. The analogy 'compute-organelle : cell :: brain : organism' is a reading offered by the framework; the cited authors do not use this framing.
sonnet_survey.uncentered_note: This synthesis was constructed holding both poles. The pro-cell-autonomy pole (Rajan 2022 habituation, Bavencoffe 2024 isolated nociceptors, evolutionary pre-neural signaling) and the skeptical pole (no confirmed associative learning by independent replication, Physarum syncytial caveat, mechanism-unknown limitation on habituation) were both given full treatment. The F254 conjecture is consistent with the literature but not established by it. Key areas where the evidence is genuinely contested or thin: (1) associative conditioning in any protist — not confirmed; (2) the exact mechanism of Physarum habituation — not known; (3) Stentor roeseli decision hierarchy mechanism — 'I can't think of any known mechanism' (Gunawardena, quoted in EurekAlert release); (4) whether state-persistence (nociceptor, CPEB) is the SAME phenomenon as 'learning' or a related but distinct cellular capacity. The 2026 Stentor associative learning preprint (bioRxiv 2026.02.25.708045) was found but content not accessed — if real and replicates, it would substantially strengthen the cell-autonomy case, but as a preprint it cannot be treated as established. Penrose-Hameroff quantum-consciousness: found no evidence this surfaced in the literature reviewed; not relevant to the single-cell learning question addressed here.

The difference is over-supply/assertion-confidence, not fabrication: SONNET asserted more as established and packed more load-bearing numbers behind citations whose own metadata it got wrong.

merged_findings.item: Stentor 2019 — behavioral hierarchy / sequential decision (NOT learning)
merged_findings.claim: Dexter, Prabakaran & Gunawardena (2019, Current Biology) confirmed a hierarchical, sequential avoidance program in the single-celled, MONONUCLEATE ciliate Stentor ROESELI (replicating Jennings 1906 and correcting a 1967 non-replication that had used the wrong species, S. coeruleus). Stereotyped partial order: bending/ciliary alteration -> contraction -> detachment, with later responses recruited only after earlier ones are exhausted; detachment never occurred without prior contraction. Headline result: the late-stage choice between contraction and detachment 'is consistent with a fair coin toss' (~50/50; probabilistic, history-dependent). Authors EXPLICITLY frame this as 'sequential decision-making' / 'behavioral hierarchy' and DISTINGUISH it from habituation or classical conditioning — it is NOT learning in the Thompson-Spencer sense. Gunawardena acknowledged no known mechanism explains how a single cell implements the hierarchy. CITATION CORRECTION (both twins caught): the task-prompt third author 'Marshall' and species 'coeruleus' are WRONG; verified third author is Jeremy Gunawardena and species is S. roeseli — the Marshall/coeruleus pairing belongs to the separate 2023 habituation paper. CAVEAT: detailed formal statistics (chi-square, exact transition probabilities, n-per-condition) were not recovered from primary full text (paywall on body); the qualitative hierarchy and ~50/50 split are confirmed via abstract + multiple independent summaries.
merged_findings.best_citation: Joseph P. Dexter, Sudhakaran Prabakaran, Jeremy Gunawardena. 'A Complex Hierarchy of Avoidance Behaviors in a Single-Cell Eukaryote.' Current Biology 29(24):4323-4329.e2 (2019). DOI 10.1016/j.cub.2019.10.059; PMID 31813604.

merged_findings.item: Stentor 2023 — genuine non-associative LEARNING (habituation) in a single cell
merged_findings.claim: Rajan, Makushok, Kalish et al. (Marshall lab, 2023, Current Biology) demonstrated HABITUATION (non-associative learning) in single Stentor coeruleus cells under calibrated mechanical stimulation, meeting Thompson & Spencer hallmarks: stimulus/frequency/intensity dependence and spontaneous recovery (~15 min). Key mechanistic finding: habituation in an INDIVIDUAL cell is a single STEP-LIKE binary switch from responsive to non-responsive (modeled as a two-state stochastic machine sensitive to the input time-series), NOT a gradual decline; population-level gradation arises from the distribution of switch times across cells. Quantitative detail (from Sonnet's PMC full-text fetch, treat as paraphrase pending verbatim re-check): contraction probability declined from ~95% (stimulus 1) to ~20-30% (stimulus 30) at high force / 1-min intervals; 20/22 cells showed statistically significant step-like switching (p<0.02); ~90% recovered after 15 min rest; forgetting rate (~0.15/min) ~150-fold faster than habituation rate (~0.001/min). Controls excluded mechanical exhaustion and local receptor adaptation (whole-cell habituation from local stimulation). This is the cleanest single-cell LEARNING datum because habituation is the accepted-as-real category AND this is a true MONONUCLEATE single cell. CITATION NOTE: Sonnet mis-cited this as 2022 / Curr. Biol. 32(24) / DOI ...11.048 despite claiming a direct PMC fetch; the verified metadata (below) is Opus's and was confirmed independently here against PubMed (PMID 36435177).
merged_findings.best_citation: Deepa Rajan, Tatyana Makushok, Asa Kalish, ..., Mark M. Slabodnick, Wallace F. Marshall. 'Single-cell analysis of habituation in Stentor coeruleus.' Current Biology 33(2):241-251.e4 (2023). DOI 10.1016/j.cub.2022.11.010; PMID 36435177; PMC9877177.

merged_findings.item: Stentor 2026 — associative (Pavlovian) learning claim in a single cell (PREPRINT, not peer-reviewed)
merged_findings.claim: A 2026 bioRxiv preprint 'Associative learning in the protozoan Stentor coeruleus' reports that temporally pairing a weak and a strong mechanical stimulus yields a TRANSIENTLY enhanced contraction response to the weak stimulus alone, which the authors interpret as associative (Pavlovian-like) conditioning in a single cell. They report a systematic dependence on inter-trial and inter-stimulus intervals (though NOT in the classical animal form) and fit a combined associative-learning + habituation model that explains why the enhancement is transient. LOAD-BEARING STATUS: this is the FIRST modern associative-single-cell claim with an accompanying quantitative model, sitting exactly at the contested frontier (associative single-cell learning is otherwise unestablished). It is a NON-peer-reviewed preprint — EXISTS and abstract-level content verified, but cannot be treated as established. The unusual DOI prefix (10.64898) is bioRxiv's genuine current prefix, NOT a hallucinated identifier. Sonnet surfaced this item (Opus missed it) and correctly flagged it low-confidence/unverified.
merged_findings.best_citation: 'Associative learning in the protozoan Stentor coeruleus.' bioRxiv 2026.02.25.708045 (v1), 2026. https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.02.25.708045v1 . PREPRINT — NOT peer reviewed; authors not extracted (PDF body returned HTTP 403).

merged_findings.claim: Nakagaki, Yamada & Toth (2000, Nature) showed the acellular plasmodium of Physarum polycephalum finds the minimum-length path through a maze between two food sources (~8 h), selecting the shortest or second-shortest path (differing ~2%) in 14 of 19 trials, by selective tube remodeling (dead-end tubes shrink; the connecting path is reinforced). This is NOT learning by any standard definition — it is analog network/path optimization physically embodied in the organism's body, framed in the letter title as 'intelligence' loosely. Same multinucleate-syncytium caveat applies (see dedicated finding).
merged_findings.best_citation: Toshiyuki Nakagaki, Hiroyasu Yamada, Agota Toth. 'Maze-solving by an amoeboid organism.' Nature 407(6803):470 (2000). DOI 10.1038/35035159; PMID 11028990.

merged_findings.item: Physarum habituation + spontaneous recovery (non-associative learning) (Boisseau, Vogel & Dussutour 2016)
merged_findings.claim: Boisseau, Vogel & Dussutour (2016, Proc. R. Soc. B) reported habituation in Physarum polycephalum: crossing a bridge laced with harmless bitter repellents (quinine or caffeine), plasmodia progressively reduced avoidance over ~6-9 days, then showed spontaneous recovery after stimulus withdrawal (~2 days). They used STIMULUS SPECIFICITY (quinine-habituated plasmodia still avoided caffeine and vice versa) to rule out sensory adaptation / generalized motor fatigue; the three criteria (response decrement, spontaneous recovery, stimulus specificity) match Thompson & Spencer (1966). Authors call it 'habituation, an unmistakable form of learning.' LOAD-BEARING CAVEAT: Physarum is a single cell by membrane but MULTINUCLEATE / acellular plasmodium — complicating a clean single-cell-cognition claim (see dedicated finding). No independent replication was identified in either twin's search; the exact enumeration of which Thompson-Spencer criteria were formally satisfied is paraphrase from fetched full text, not verbatim.
merged_findings.best_citation: Romain P. Boisseau, David Vogel, Audrey Dussutour. 'Habituation in non-neural organisms: evidence from slime moulds.' Proceedings of the Royal Society B 283(1829):20160446 (2016). DOI 10.1098/rspb.2016.0446; PMC4855389.

merged_findings.item: Physarum memory transfer by cell fusion (Vogel & Dussutour 2016)
merged_findings.claim: Vogel & Dussutour (2016, Proc. R. Soc. B) reported that a habituated (e.g. salt/quinine-trained) Physarum plasmodium can transfer the acquired behaviour to a NAIVE plasmodium by fusing with it; the fused organism crosses the repellent faster than naive controls (>2,000 plasmodia trained). Offered as direct transfer of a learned state via cytoplasmic fusion. CAVEATS: (a) mechanism is unidentified — could be a small molecule / phosphorylation / expression state rather than a packaged 'memory'; (b) same multinucleate-syncytium complication; (c) 'transfer' is cell-cell cytoplasmic fusion, not an isolated-and-reinjected memory molecule; (d) no independent replication identified. CITATION NOTE: venue is Proc. R. Soc. B (not Current Biology as the task prompt implied for some Physarum work) — confirmed.
merged_findings.best_citation: David Vogel, Audrey Dussutour. 'Direct transfer of learned behaviour via cell fusion in non-neural organisms.' Proceedings of the Royal Society B 283(1845):20162382 (2016). DOI 10.1098/rspb.2016.2382; PMID 28003457; PMC5204175.

merged_findings.item: CRITICAL CAVEAT — is Physarum a 'single cell'? (the multinucleate-syncytium complication)
merged_findings.claim: Physarum polycephalum in plasmodial form is a SYNCYTIUM: one continuous cytoplasm containing thousands-to-millions of nuclei with NO internal cell membranes, arising from amoeba fusion + mitosis without cytokinesis, and reaching cm-to-tens-of-cm scale. It is one cell by the absence-of-membranes criterion but carries a multicellular-scale genome complement in one cytoplasm. This is a LOAD-BEARING complication for every Physarum 'single-cell cognition' claim above: (a) integration may be inter-nuclear via shared cytoplasm — qualitatively unlike processing within a mononucleate cell; (b) the spatial scale far exceeds a typical cell; (c) critics can read Physarum habituation/transfer as network-level dynamics of a distributed syncytium rather than cell-intrinsic computation, while proponents counter that the single shared cytoplasm IS the relevant unit. The debate is genuine and unresolved. (This caveat is asserted by the survey as a structural fact of cell biology; the syncytial nature itself is uncontested, the cognition implication is a reading widely noted in review literature.)
merged_findings.best_citation: Syncytial/multinucleate structure is uncontested standard cell biology (no single primary source attests the cognition controversy specifically). The complication is noted across review literature; e.g. discussions in non-neural-cognition reviews and Moroz LL, 'Multiple Origins of Neurons From Secretory Cells,' Front. Cell Dev. Biol. 9:669087 (2021), PMC8293673 (syncytial/secretory-cell context). FLAG: distributed across sources, not a single attesting DOI.

merged_findings.item: THE SKEPTICAL POLE — Gershman, Balbi, Gallistel & Gunawardena 2021 (eLife): reconsideration, NOT vindication
merged_findings.claim: Gershman, Balbi, Gallistel & Gunawardena (2021, eLife) ACCEPT non-associative learning (habituation) in single cells as established/uncontroversial and accept the Stentor roeseli hierarchy as genuine. Their CONTESTED move is to argue for REHABILITATING associative (Pavlovian) single-cell learning: re-examining Beatrice Gelber's 1950s Paramecium aurelia conditioning, they conclude her experiments 'though not without their limitations, convincingly demonstrated Pavlovian conditioning in Paramecia,' and reinterpret the classic critiques — Jensen's thigmotropism/bacteria-contamination account, and Katz & Deterline's 'stirring' control — as methodological deviations / 'contingency degradation' (CS-US decorrelation, which suppresses conditioning in ANY system) rather than refutations. They suggest molecular storage (DNA methylation, histone modification) over synaptic plasticity. CRUCIAL FOR BALANCE: this paper is itself a CONTESTED MINORITY position — it argues FOR reconsidering, it does NOT settle the question and runs against prevailing consensus. (Whether the paper critically addresses Physarum habituation specifically is unconfirmed; its focus is Paramecium.)
merged_findings.best_citation: Samuel J. Gershman, Petra E.M. Balbi, C. Randy Gallistel, Jeremy Gunawardena. 'Reconsidering the evidence for learning in single cells.' eLife 10:e61907 (2021). DOI 10.7554/eLife.61907; PMID 33395388; PMC7781593.

merged_findings.item: THE SKEPTICAL POLE — associative/Pavlovian single-cell learning is contested and largely unreplicated
merged_findings.claim: Historical associative-learning claims in Paramecium have a POOR replication record: (a) Gelber's Pavlovian results (1950s) — Katz & Deterline (1958) reportedly FAILED to replicate; Jensen (1957) gave a bacteria/thigmotropism alternative; (b) Hennessey, Rucker & McDiarmid (1979, Animal Learning & Behavior) reported classical conditioning (vibration CS + shock US, with Rescorla random controls) in Paramecium caudatum, NEVER independently replicated; (c) Armus, Montgomery & Gurney (2006) reported brightness-discrimination learning but the design has a documented light-dark counterbalance confound, with only a PARTIAL later replication (Alipour et al. 2018). NET, field status 2024-2026: NON-associative single-cell learning (habituation) is accepted as real; ASSOCIATIVE (Pavlovian/operant) single-cell learning remains UNSETTLED with no robust independent replication of the foundational claims; Gershman et al. 2021 is the minority pro-reconsideration position; the 2026 Stentor preprint is a new (non-peer-reviewed) entry at this frontier. CONFIDENCE: the qualitative 'associative single-cell learning is contested/unreplicated' is HIGH (it is the literature's own framing); the PRECISE replication history (Katz & Deterline failed-to-replicate, Hennessey never-replicated, Armus confound, Alipour partial) is MEDIUM — sourced from web summaries and Gershman et al.'s recounting, NOT from independent primary fetch of Katz & Deterline 1958, Jensen 1957, or Alipour 2018.
merged_findings.best_citation: Hennessey, Rucker & McDiarmid, 'Classical conditioning in paramecia,' Animal Learning & Behavior 7(4):417-423 (1979), DOI 10.3758/BF03209695. Armus, Montgomery & Gurney, 'Discrimination Learning and Extinction in Paramecia (P. caudatum),' Psychological Reports 98(3):705-711 (2006), DOI 10.2466/pr0.98.3.705-711. Gelber controversy / Katz & Deterline 1958 / Jensen 1957 as recounted in Gershman et al. 2021 (PMC7781593).

merged_findings.item: Cell-intrinsic molecular memory — Walters 2012 (the vertebrate state-persistence bridge)
merged_findings.claim: Walters (2012, Front. Physiol.) — a HYPOTHESIS-AND-THEORY article (not a primary data paper) — argues the spinal-cord-injury-induced hyperexcitable / spontaneously-active (HSA) state of nociceptors PERSISTS in DISSOCIATED, low-density culture lacking serum or growth factors (expressed ~1 day after dissociation, at ~35-70% incidence from 3 days to 8+ months post-injury), i.e. the persistent excitability state is INTRINSIC TO THE INDIVIDUAL CELL, not dependent on circuit or tissue; Walters uses 'cellular memory within nociceptors' and invokes hyperalgesic priming. KEY DISTINCTION (do not conflate): this is STATE-PERSISTENCE / hysteresis of an already-induced functional state, a DIFFERENT sense from associative/non-associative LEARNING (no stimulus-contingent acquisition is shown in the dish). Strong evidence for cell-resident, circuit-independent state storage; NOT evidence for single-cell learning per se.
merged_findings.best_citation: Edgar T. Walters. 'Nociceptors as chronic drivers of pain and hyperreflexia after spinal cord injury: an adaptive-maladaptive hyperfunctional state hypothesis.' Frontiers in Physiology 3:309 (2012). DOI 10.3389/fphys.2012.00309; PMID 22934060; PMC3429080.

merged_findings.item: Cell-intrinsic molecular memory — Bavencoffe/Walters 2024: cAMP-induced long-term hyperexcitability in ISOLATED nociceptors (PEER-REVIEWED)
merged_findings.claim: Bavencoffe, Zhu, Neerukonda, Johnson, Dessauer & Walters (2024) directly tested intrinsic cellular state-persistence in DISSOCIATED DRG nociceptors from naive (uninjured) rats: 6-hour treatment with prucalopride (Gas-coupled 5-HT4 agonist, 1 uM) or forskolin (adenylyl cyclase activator) induced long-term hyperexcitability (LTH) persisting 12-24 h after washout, in isolated cells with no circuit connections. Reported quantities (from Sonnet's PMC fetch; treat statistics as paraphrase pending verbatim re-check): ongoing activity at -45 mV in 0-8% of vehicle cells vs 37-50% prucalopride (Fisher's exact p<0.05); resting potential depolarized ~-69 -> -66 mV (p<0.05); PKA-, CREB-, transcription-, and protein-synthesis-inhibitors all abolished LTH (Bonferroni-corrected p<0.025 to 0.0005, 17 experiments). Authors link it to 'a prototypical cellular signaling pathway previously found to induce memory-related synaptic LTP.' DISTINCTION: this is STATE-PERSISTENCE induced by a pharmacological trigger in isolated cells (hysteresis sense of 'cellular memory'), NOT learning (no CS-US pairing). MAJOR CORRECTION TO BOTH TWINS: Sonnet (and the comparison) listed this as a bioRxiv preprint only; it is in fact PEER-REVIEWED PUBLISHED in Neurobiology of Pain 16:100166 (2024), PMID 39399224 — a STRONGER attestation than either twin claimed. Sonnet surfaced this item; Opus missed it.
merged_findings.best_citation: Alexis Bavencoffe, Michael Y. Zhu, Sanjay V. Neerukonda, Kayla N. Johnson, Carmen W. Dessauer, Edgar T. Walters. 'Induction of long-term hyperexcitability by memory-related cAMP signaling in isolated nociceptor cell bodies.' Neurobiology of Pain 16:100166 (2024). DOI 10.1016/j.ynpai.2024.100166; PMID 39399224; PMC11470187. (Earlier as bioRxiv 2024.07.13.603393.)

merged_findings.item: Cell-intrinsic molecular memory — CPEB prion-like translational state (Bogen et al. 2012 + Si/Kandel lineage + Fioriti 2015)
merged_findings.claim: A self-sustaining prion-like translational state is a candidate cell-autonomous molecular-memory substrate. (1) Si, Lindquist & Kandel (2003, Cell) identified a neuronal Aplysia CPEB isoform with prion-like properties that self-perpetuates an aggregated, active conformation at stimulated synapses, maintaining synapse-specific long-term facilitation. (2) Bogen, Alessandri-Haber, Chu, Gear & Levine (2012, J. Neurosci.) extended this to the peripheral nociceptor: PKCepsilon-mediated activation of CPEB generates a long-lasting 'pain memory' (hyperalgesic priming requiring ~72 h to establish); authors frame a self-perpetuating CPEB conformer as a form of pain memory. (3) Fioriti et al. (2015, Neuron) showed mouse CPEB3 ablation impairs maintenance of hippocampal LTP and spatial memory. DISTINCTION: like Walters, this is SELF-SUSTAINING STATE PERSISTENCE (molecular bistability/self-templating), a different sense from learning; it is the MECHANISM by which a cell could hold a state cell-autonomously. CRITICAL CITATION RESOLUTION: Opus cited Bogen 2012 correctly; SONNET WRONGLY declared 'Bogen & Levine 2012' NOT FOUND / a prompt error and proposed a wrong substitute (Pavlopoulos et al., 'Neuralized1 activates CPEB3'). Independent verification here confirms Bogen et al. 2012 is REAL and exact (J. Neurosci. landing page) — Sonnet's nullification is rejected.
merged_findings.best_citation: Oliver Bogen, Nicole Alessandri-Haber, Carissa Chu, Robert W. Gear, Jon D. Levine. 'Generation of a Pain Memory in the Primary Afferent Nociceptor Triggered by PKCepsilon Activation of CPEB.' Journal of Neuroscience 32(6):2018-2026 (2012). DOI 10.1523/JNEUROSCI.5138-11.2012. (Lineage: Si, Lindquist & Kandel, 'A neuronal isoform of the Aplysia CPEB has prion-like properties,' Cell 115(7):879-891 (2003), DOI 10.1016/S0092-8674(03)01022-5, PMID 14697205; Fioriti et al., Neuron 86(6):1433-1448 (2015), PMID 26074003.)

merged_findings.item: Single-cell epigenetic / transcriptional memory and bet-hedging (state-persistence, not learning)
merged_findings.claim: Single cells maintain heritable transcriptional states via (a) bistable gene-regulatory circuits with feedback, (b) chromatin modification (histone marks, DNA methylation) propagated through mitosis, and (c) stochastic state-switching (bet-hedging). A cell can thus 'remember' a prior exposure (e.g. faster reactivation of a previously-activated gene = transcriptional memory, established in yeast and mammalian cells; reviews note accelerated reactivation via chromatin changes + poised Pol II). These are STATE-PERSISTENCE (hysteresis) mechanisms, NOT learning (no contingency-based modification of future responding). They establish that cell-intrinsic molecular memory in the hysteresis sense is real and widespread. CAVEAT: this is a well-established general mechanism, but Sonnet's specific primary citations were NOT individually verified at DOI level (the named review 'Establishment and inheritance of epigenetic transcriptional memory,' PMC9479176, and the Kaufmann & van Oudenaarden reference were flagged by Sonnet itself as unconfirmed). Treat the general mechanism as established; verify exact citations before lodging as AMSC entries. Opus did not surface this item.
merged_findings.best_citation: General mechanism well-established in cell biology; specific primary citations UNVERIFIED at DOI level (e.g. review at PMC9479176, 2022; Kaufmann & van Oudenaarden, Curr. Opin. Cell Biol.). FLAG: confirm full citations before attestation.

merged_findings.item: Origin-of-neurons reading — neurons specialized an ancestral cell-general signalling toolkit (Burkhardt 2015; Arendt 2016; Burkhardt & Sprecher 2017; Moroz 2014/2016/2021)
merged_findings.claim: Substantial evolutionary-neuroscience literature treats the neuron as a cell that SPECIALIZED an ancestral, cell-general signalling/secretory capacity ('synaptic genes predate synapses'): (1) Burkhardt (2015, J. Exp. Biol.) — choanoflagellates (closest unicellular animal relatives) carry diverse synaptic-protein homologs incl. a primordial neurosecretory apparatus; most synaptic proteins evolved BEFORE neurons. (2) Arendt et al. (2016, Nat. Rev. Genet.) — 'sister cell type' model: neurons and other cell types descend from shared precursors by divergence of a core regulatory complex. (3) Burkhardt & Sprecher (2017, BioEssays) — neuron-less sponges, placozoans, and unicellular choanoflagellates express homologs of key neuronal/synaptic proteins; a shared primordial secretory/sensory ancestor is plausible. (4) Moroz et al. (2014, Nature) + Moroz (2016, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B; 2021, Front. Cell Dev. Biol.) — ctenophore genomics support INDEPENDENT (convergent, polygenetic) origins of neural systems, implying the underlying excitable/signalling toolkit is ancestral and repeatedly co-opted. CAVEAT (both twins agree): these support 'neurons specialize an ancestral cell-general toolkit' but make NO claim about a within-cell 'compute-organelle,' and do NOT on their own support the scale-recursive 'brain:organism::compute-organelle:cell' mapping — that mapping is FRAMEWORK-READING (a LENS), not the cited authors' assertion. Penrose-Hameroff quantum-microtubule consciousness did NOT surface in the verified primary literature; flagged fringe/out-of-scope (not affirmatively searched-and-refuted, by design).
